newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's CDC bank lowers Q496, Q197 growth outlook.
newsitem.headline: France's CDC bank lowers Q496, Q197 growth outlook.

text.p: French state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) on Monday lowered its estimate for French economic growth to 0.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from 0.3 percent previously.
CDC also lowered its estimate for first quarter growth in 1997 to 0.4 percent from 0.5 percent.

CDC said in a statement, "The slowing of economic activity from the third quarter, where growth came in at 0.9 percent, is confirmed. The reasons behind the slowdown remain intact: a 0.8 percent decline in manufacturing consumption and a deteriorating labour market."
The seasonally adjusted figures are based on a leading indicator composed of data published up to December 31, 1996.

It also said its indicator showed "moderate improvement" in the first quarter of 1997, "essentially due to a favourable interest rate environment. Although the easing of interest rates continues at a slower pace than at the beginning of 1996, it nonetheless continues to support the indicator."
CDC said the estimates were a synthetic index, not a forecast.
